summary.headline: Bajaj Finserv Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 5% to INR 2,539 crores, which management says is 24% ex-temporary FVTPL MTM losses at insurers.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income grew 6% to about INR 38,508 crores, which management attributes to temporary FVTPL mark-to-market losses at the insurance subsidiaries from geopolitical tensions; ex-MTM, revenue growth is put at 14%. Bajaj General's GWP was flat at INR 4,322 crores, with a combined ratio of 113.6% due to a retro-dated government health treaty and lower crop business, while Bajaj Life's VNB rose 29% to INR 709 crores with NBM at 24.5%. Bajaj Finance and Bajaj Housing Finance reported strong growth, with BFL AUM crossing INR 5 lakh crores. The Allianz 3% stake buyback was completed in March, and both insurers will seek a one-year Ind AS forbearance.

segments.name: Bajaj General Insurance
segments.commentary: GWP flat at INR 4,322 crores on tactical cuts in crop and motor amid pricing pressure; underwriting loss INR 96 crores; AUM INR 35,529 crores (+7.3%); solvency 302%; ROE ex-surplus capital about 18.5%.

segments.name: Bajaj Life Insurance
segments.commentary: Retail protection share 8.4% of retail business (protection growing 67%); renewal premium +18%; GWP +21%; persistency dipped in certain cohorts; solvency 266%; AUM INR 1,33,563 crores (+8%).

segments.name: Bajaj Finance
segments.commentary: Record quarter: new loans 1.29 crores (+20%), net total income INR 14,209 crores (+21%), loan losses and provisions INR 2,008 crores; CRAR 21.55%.

segments.name: Bajaj Housing Finance
segments.commentary: AUM growth 22.7%; NII INR 945 crores (+15%); Opex to NTI 19.2% (vs 21.8%); GNPA 0.27%; CRAR 22.46%.

segments.name: Bajaj Finserv Health
segments.commentary: About 6.5 million healthcare transactions (vs 5.3 million); revenue +41.6%; management guides to operating break-even in about 24 months.

segments.name: Bajaj Finserv Markets (Bajaj Markets)
segments.commentary: Operating revenue fell to about INR 95 crores from INR 129 crores on planned platform migration; disbursements INR 2,047 crores (vs INR 1,800 crores in Q3); about 103 partners; break-even targeted around end-FY27.

segments.name: Bajaj Finserv AMC
segments.commentary: Ranked 26th among mutual fund AMCs by AUM; break-even AUM estimated at about INR 1 lakh crore; PMS and SIF launches planned within 1-1.5 years.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Bajaj Life growth to be better than its H2 FY26 growth, with bancassurance partners Federal, AU and Yes Bank expected to contribute.
Bajaj Life will not provide margin guidance; management says the VNB margin trajectory is positive, with term share targeted at 10%+ and ULIP at about 40%.
Management says ~90-92% of the annualised ~4.5% GST impact on Bajaj Life was mitigated by March 2026, leaving a 30-40 bps residual.
Both insurers will seek IRDAI forbearance and transition to Ind AS from 1 April 2027.
Bajaj Finserv Health expects operating break-even in about 24 months; Bajaj Markets targets break-even around end of FY27.
PMS launch expected within the next two quarters; CAT II/III AIF approvals (PE and real estate) are expected within about one quarter.
capex_capacity: Allianz 3% stake buyback in the insurers completed in March 2026; one-time impact on solvency and AUM was about INR 1,590 crores at Bajaj General and about INR 1,200 crores at Bajaj Life.
Post-buyback holding of insurers: 77.33% Bajaj Finserv, 18.10% Bajaj Holdings, about 4.60% Jamnalal Sons.
Bajaj Finance is accelerating gold loan branch expansion; AI investments are weighing on the opex ratio.
Bajaj Finserv Health provider network: about 130,000+ doctors, 15,000+ hospitals, 6,500+ lab touchpoints.
Bajaj General reinsurance cover (CAT) is said to be double the industry benchmark on a 1-in-year return basis.
demand_pricing: Bajaj General: management is slowing growth in crop and motor where pricing is inadequate; industry combined ratio rose about 6-7 pp in FY26 and touched 128% in one quarter, while Bajaj General's combined ratio rose only 0.5 pp.
Bajaj Life product mix (retail weighted received premium): PAR 25%, non-par savings and annuity 24%, term 8%, ULIP 42%. Annuity share doubled from 5% to 10%; non-par fell from 21% to 16%.
Bajaj Life persistency fell in certain cohorts in line with the sector, linked to early-gratification products launched by market leaders 12-18 months ago; the product has been stopped since October.
Bajaj Finance: 1.29 crore new loans; management says business-loan manufacturer risk-tightening affects Bajaj Markets' partner mix but not its volumes or revenue.
Competitive intensity is elevated in motor, group health (GMC) and fire, partly due to insurers above 30% EOM ramping volumes ahead of EOM guidelines.
Bajaj General health growth was 30% in Q4 vs industry 18.1%; industry retail health grew about 17%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the motor TP reserve release rise to about INR 800 crores vs INR 600-700 crores in prior years?
qa_highlights.answer: Tapan Singhel said TP is a long-tail book; the release reflects claims development against reserving, and he sees no shift in reserving philosophy, implying the company has adequately reserved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bajaj Life VNB margin outlook and product mix target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Vipin Bansal said margin expansion reflects product and channel mix, payout management and about 150 bps from cost efforts. Target mix: PAR about 25%, annuity plus non-par 25-30%, term 10%+, ULIP about 40%. Management declined to guide to a FY27 margin level.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 22% pre-GST VNB margin repeat in FY27 with the same mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Tarun Chugh declined to affirm any margin; he said the trajectory is positive and that mitigation benefits are embedded in the 636 bps margin walk, with INR 242 crores as the gross GST dent.

qa_highlights.question: How does Bajaj Life expect growth to trend in FY27, and where will it come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Tarun Chugh expects better growth than H2 FY26 (about mid-teens), with agency up 8% QoQ for two quarters, bancassurance partners ramping, and proprietary and direct channels expected to grow faster.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bajaj Alternatives strategy and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramandeep Sahni said SEBI has approved the listed-equity PMS, filings are in for PE and real estate CAT II/III AIFs, products should roll out over the next two quarters, and a GIFT City structure is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for life insurance commission changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Tarun Chugh said no draft circular has been received from IRDAI; the mood appears to favour back-ending commissions, which would benefit the sector if implemented.

qa_highlights.question: Why not publish IFRS 17 numbers now?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramandeep Sahni said ambiguity on level of aggregation, tax and opening adjustments makes publishing premature for a multi-line group; the company is awaiting regulator clarity and expects publication from 1 April 2027.

risks_watch: Persistency decline in Bajaj Life: management says cohorts dipped in line with sector after early-gratification products; sector degrowth of about 1.8% cited; watch persistency recovery and the 'persistency already baked in' EV assumption change of INR 51 crores.

Bajaj General pricing discipline: management is slowing crop and motor where pricing is inadequate, so growth could stay muted; combined ratio of 113.6% in Q4 includes a retro-dated government health treaty and timing variance on claims.
Life insurance commission restructuring (back-ending) under discussion; no IRDAI draft circular received yet, so the impact on distribution costs and VNB is unquantified.
Ind AS transition for both insurers from 1 April 2027 after one-year forbearance; IFRS 17 numbers not yet published pending regulator clarity on level of aggregation, tax and opening adjustments.

Bajaj Finserv Markets revenue fell to about INR 95 crores from INR 129 crores; break-even target around end-FY27 depends on trail revenue ramp, and Bajaj Finserv Health break-even is guided at about 24 months.
Motor TP reserve release of about INR 800 crores vs INR 600-700 crores in prior years; management says no change in reserving philosophy but this is a long-tail book to monitor.
key_quotes: So, just to summarize, both the revenue and the bottom line for the quarter being reported are largely impacted by the MTM impact, which we believe is temporary in nature due to the geopolitical risk.
We will, not provide any affirmation or otherwise from us on margins if you're going to indicate like this, please.
I think it's too early to start publishing these numbers.
So it's really an impact on the market, there's nothing to do with the pricing etc. as of now from our side.
summary.management_tone: Management is confident on the underlying franchise and on Bajaj Life's margin trajectory, but cautious and evasive on forward numbers: Tarun Chugh declined to affirm any FY27 VNB margin, and Ramandeep Sahni declined to publish IFRS 17 numbers pending regulator clarity. On General Insurance, management is defensive about the 113.6% Q4 combined ratio, attributing it to timing and a retro-dated treaty, while stressing pricing discipline.

adds.what: Bajaj Finserv Health provider network expansion (130,000+ doctors, 15,000+ hospitals, 6,500+ lab touchpoints); not a capacity addition with a stated number
Bajaj Finance accelerating gold loan branch expansion (no branch count given)
PMS launch within next two quarters (AMC product launch, not productive capacity)

growth.why: No explicit numeric revenue growth guidance; management expects Bajaj Life growth above H2 FY26 pace backed by bancassurance partners (Federal, AU, Yes Bank), Life VNB up 29% to INR 709 crores, and Bajaj Finance AUM +22% with a record quarter, while Bajaj General GWP was flat and growth is being slowed in unprofitable crop and motor.
